title: The Jewish Year
objective: After this level you can explain the meaning and customs of Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Passover, Sukkot and Hanukkah.
summary: Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur bring the shofar, repentance and a fast. Sukkot recalls the wilderness, Passover retells the Exodus, Hanukkah remembers a rededicated Temple.

cards.headline: The Jewish year opens with a blast on a ram's horn.
cards.body: Then come ten serious days, meals in a hut, a dinner full of questions and eight nights of lights. Each festival tells part of the Jewish story.

cards.headline: New year, clean slate
cards.body: Rosh Hashanah, the religious New Year, falls on 1 Tishri, in September or October. The shofar, a ram's horn, sounds a call to spiritual reawakening. It opens the Ten Days of Repentance, which end on Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement: the holiest day of the year, with a 25-hour fast and prayer. Beforehand, friends ask each other's forgiveness, since forgiveness from people signifies forgiveness from God.

cards.headline: A hut and a question-filled dinner
cards.body: Five days after Yom Kippur comes Sukkot. Families eat, and some even sleep, in huts roofed with branches, recalling the Israelites' 40 years in the wilderness. In March or April, Passover remembers the escape from slavery in Egypt: at the seder, people read the story from the Haggadah, and children ask, "Why does this night differ from all other nights?" Matzah recalls dough that had no time to rise.

cards.headline: Eight nights of light
cards.body: Hanukkah, "dedication", remembers the Maccabees rededicating the Second Temple in 164 BCE. One more candle is lit each night for eight nights, and the Talmud tells of oil that burned for eight days. Big glow, small holiday: it has traditionally counted as minor, and it isn't in the Hebrew Bible.

cards.headline: The Jewish Year: the takeaways
learned: Rosh Hashanah opens ten days of repentance that end on Yom Kippur
Sukkot and Passover recall the wilderness and the Exodus
Hanukkah remembers the rededication of the Second Temple

questions.prompt: Put these holy days in the order they come, starting from the New Year.
questions.explanation: Rosh Hashanah opens the Ten Days of Repentance, which end on Yom Kippur. Sukkot comes five days after Yom Kippur.

questions.prompt: Why do friends ask each other for forgiveness before Yom Kippur?

options.label: Because the fast is not allowed until debts are paid
options.rationale: The point is forgiveness, not money.

options.label: Because forgiveness from people signifies God's forgiveness
Because Rosh Hashanah forbids speaking to friends
options.rationale: Rosh Hashanah has no such rule.

options.label: Because the Temple priests required a list of names

questions.explanation: Obtaining forgiveness from one's fellows signifies God's forgiveness, so it comes first.

questions.prompt: Sukkot huts and Passover matzah both point back to which Level 12 story?

options.label: The escape from Egypt and the years in the wilderness
Abraham's journey from Ur to Canaan
The return from exile in Babylon
The Maccabees' rededication of the Temple

questions.explanation: Passover retells the escape from Egypt, and Sukkot recalls the 40 years in the wilderness that followed.
